To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

women experiencing IPV are more likely to disclose IPV to medical professionals if they experience 31 or more episodes of physical IPV in the preceding year, have needed medical services for the violence, have experienced an IPV related injury, have two or more health problems (other than IPV), are fearful of their partners, have poor mental health, have been unable to see a doctor due to financial reasons, and are 55 years of age or older.

women's likelihood of telling medical professionals about intimate partner violence is increased when they have experienced a high number of physical intimate partner violence episodes in the past year; have needed medical services for intimate partner violence; have been injured by intimate partner violence; fear their intimate partner; have 2 or more chronic health problems, or poor mental health; or are older than 55.
women who experience more physical IPV episodes are more likely to tell their medical providers about their abuse.
